## Why another language? 🤔 {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Python** 🐍

- General purpose
- Files, pipelines, automation
- Sequences and text 🧬
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**R** 🇷

- Built by statisticians, for data
- Tables, statistics, plots 📊
- Bioconductor: RNA-seq, microarrays
:::
::::

. . .

You will meet R in almost every biology lab. 💛

::: notes
0–10 min. Honest framing: not better or worse, different default job.
:::

## Good news: you already know this {.smaller}

| Concept | Python | R |
|---|---|---|
| Assign | `x = 5` | `x <- 5` |
| Comment | `# note` | `# note` |
| Function | `len(x)` | `length(x)` |
| Condition | `if x > 5:` | `if (x > 5) {` |
| Loop | `for s in seqs:` | `for (s in seqs) {` |
| Math on all | `np.array(x) * 2` | `x * 2` |
| Table | `pd.DataFrame(...)` | `data.frame(...)` |

. . .

New syntax, same **thinking**. 🧠

::: notes
10–25 min. This is the core message of the R weeks: transfer, not restart.
:::

## RStudio 🖥️ {.smaller}

Four panels:

- **Console** — try things out (like `python3` interactive)
- **Script** — your saved code 💾
- **Environment** — what variables exist right now 👀
- **Plots / Files** 📊

. . .

Run a line: **Ctrl/Cmd + Enter** ⏎

::: notes
Screen share and point at each panel. The Environment panel is something Python beginners never get — highlight it.
:::

## Vectors: R's superpower ⚡ {.smaller}

```r
lengths <- c(120, 85, 300, 42)

length(lengths)     # 4
mean(lengths)       # 136.75
max(lengths)
sort(lengths)

lengths * 2         # every element doubled — no loop! 🤯
lengths > 100       # TRUE FALSE TRUE FALSE
```

. . .

In R, operations work on **whole vectors** at once.

::: notes
Same idea as numpy arrays from week 10 — in R it is built in, no library needed.
:::

## Sounds familiar? numpy! 🐍🤝🇷 {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**numpy** 🐍 (week 10)

```python
import numpy as np
arr = np.array([120, 85, 300, 42])

len(arr)
arr.mean()
arr.max()
np.sort(arr)

arr * 2
arr > 100
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**R** 🇷

```r

lengths <- c(120, 85, 300, 42)

length(lengths)
mean(lengths)
max(lengths)
sort(lengths)

lengths * 2
lengths > 100
```
:::
::::

. . .

A vector = a numpy array that is **built in**: no `import` needed ⚡

Fun fact: R has no single numbers. `5` is a vector of length 1 → `length(5)` gives `1` 🤯

::: notes
They did numpy on 23.11, so this should click immediately. Ask them to predict each R line from the numpy one.
:::

## Indexing ⚠️ {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**numpy** 🐍

```python
arr[0]            # first element
arr[[0, 2]]       # first and third
arr[arr > 100]    # filter 🎯
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**R** 🇷

```r
lengths[1]              # first element 🤨
lengths[c(1, 3)]        # first and third
lengths[lengths > 100]  # filter 🎯
```
:::
::::

Filtering by condition: **identical** ✅ Position: **different** ⚠️

. . .

::: {.callout-warning}
Python counts from 0, R counts from 1. This will bite you. 🐛
:::

## Data frames: tables 📊 {.smaller}

```r
seqs <- data.frame(
  name   = c("seq1", "seq2", "seq3"),
  length = c(120, 85, 300),
  gc     = c(0.55, 0.41, 0.62)
)

head(seqs)          # first rows
nrow(seqs)          # number of rows
seqs$length         # one column as a vector
mean(seqs$gc)
```

. . .

| R 🇷 | pandas 🐼 |
|---|---|
| `data.frame(...)` | `pd.DataFrame({...})` |
| `head(seqs)` | `df.head()` |
| `nrow(seqs)` | `len(df)` |
| `seqs$length` → a **vector** | `df["length"]` → a **Series** |
| `mean(seqs$gc)` | `df["gc"].mean()` |

pandas was **inspired by** R's data.frame 🐼 ([McKinney, SciPy 2010](https://proceedings.scipy.org/articles/Majora-92bf1922-00a.pdf))

## Filtering rows 🎯 {.smaller}

```r
seqs[seqs$length > 100, ]          # rows where length > 100
seqs[seqs$gc > 0.5, "name"]        # just the names
seqs$gc_percent <- seqs$gc * 100   # add a new column ➕
```

. . .

| R 🇷 | pandas 🐼 |
|---|---|
| `seqs[seqs$length > 100, ]` | `df[df["length"] > 100]` |
| `seqs[seqs$gc > 0.5, "name"]` | `df.loc[df["gc"] > 0.5, "name"]` |
| `seqs$gc_percent <- seqs$gc * 100` | `df["gc_percent"] = df["gc"] * 100` |

The comma matters: `[rows, columns]`, just like `.loc[rows, columns]` 📐

## Exercise: First steps in R 🇷 {.smaller}

⏱️ 30 min · breakout rooms · switch after 15 min

In RStudio, create `scripts/first_analysis.R`:

1. Make a vector of 6 sequence lengths
2. Print the mean, max and sorted values
3. Print only the lengths above 100
4. Build a data frame with `name`, `length`, `gc` (6 rows)
5. Add a `gc_percent` column
6. Print only rows with GC above 50% 🎯

💡 **Bonus:** `summary(seqs)` — what does it give you?

::: notes
25–65 min. Paste in the chat. Expect `<-` vs `=` confusion and the missing comma in `[rows, ]`.
:::

## Wrap-up ✅ {.smaller}

| R 🇷 | Python 🐍 | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `x <- c(1,2,3)` | `np.array([1,2,3])` | vector / array |
| `mean()` `max()` `sort()` | `.mean()` `.max()` `np.sort()` | stats, no loop ⚡ |
| `df$column` | `df["column"]` | one column |
| `df[df$x > 5, ]` | `df[df["x"] > 5]` | filter rows 🎯 |

**Remember:** R counts from **1** ⚠️
